meaning:
σῦκον, -ου, τό
[in LXX for תְּאֵן ]
a fig: Mat.7:16, Mrk.11:13, Luk.6:44 Jas.3:12.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
Seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came to see if perhaps he might find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was…
For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.
Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine figs? Thus no spring yields both salt water and fresh water.
